query: FeNiCrCoCu is considered suitable for thin-film use, and its expense favors applying it as a protective coating on conventional metals rather than using it in bulk. Earlier studies examined room-temperature wear behavior in relation to coating–substrate combinations, composition, and grain size, but largely addressed the alloy itself or a limited thermal regime rather than the overall wear response of a coating across different temperatures. Under the constraints that FeNiCrCoCu remains a thin protective coating and that high-temperature wear is the target application, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs its overall wear resistance and why? Specify an intervention relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the observations expected if the hypothesis is correct, state the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, connect the hypothesis to prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: At high temperatures, the wear resistance of a thin FeNiCrCoCu coating is governed by the in situ formation of an adherent, Cr-rich oxide layer that acts as a protective barrier by pinning grain boundaries and reducing surface abrasion.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin film with a fine, homogeneous microstructure.
generation.intervention: Apply a controlled pre-oxidation treatment (e.g., heat the coating at ~600°C for 1 hour) prior to wear testing, compared with a baseline of untreated, as-deposited coatings.
generation.conditions: High-temperature wear tests performed at approximately 600°C under high loads typical for protective coating applications.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a continuous, thin Cr-rich oxide scale along the surface and at grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: At elevated temperatures, chromium in the alloy oxidizes preferentially. The resulting oxide layer adheres to the surface and grain boundaries, pinning the microstructure and acting as a barrier that both prevents further oxidation and mitigates abrasive wear by reducing direct metal-to-metal contact.
generation.predicted_outcome: If the hypothesis is correct, pre-oxidized coatings will show a significantly lower wear rate (i.e., reduced volume loss and retained hardness) during high-temperature wear tests than the as-deposited coatings. Microscopy should reveal a continuous, Cr-rich oxide layer in the pre-oxidized samples.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis applies under high-temperature conditions around 600°C with high mechanical loading; effects outside this thermal and loading window remain uncertain.
generation.uncertainty: Details such as the exact composition, optimal thickness of the oxide layer, and the performance of the oxide under temperatures significantly above 600°C need further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of FeNiCrCoCu coating samples: one set receives a pre-oxidation treatment at 600°C for 1 hour, and the other remains in the as-deposited state. Subject both sets to identical high-temperature wear tests at 600°C under high-load conditions. Characterize the wear tracks and microstructure using SEM/TEM for oxide layer continuity, measure wear volume loss, and assess hardness retention.
measurements: Wear volume loss (mass or depth removed)
Hardness before and after wear testing
Thickness and continuity of the oxide layer (via microscopy)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the pre-oxidized samples do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in wear rate or better hardness retention compared to the as-deposited samples, or if no continuous Cr-rich oxide layer is observed on the treated samples, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract WVTaTiCr x ( x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings were prepared on a 42-CrMo steel plate using laser cladding. The purpose of this work is to investigate the effect of the Cr content on the microstructure and properties of the WVTaTiCr x coating. The morphologies and phase compositions of five coatings with different Cr contents were comparatively observed. In addition, the hardness and high-temperature oxidation resistance of the coatings were also analyzed. As a result, with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined. All the coating is mainly composed of the BCC solid-solution phase, which promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase with the increase in Cr. The addition of Cr greatly improves the hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and corrosion resistance of the coating. The WVTaTiCr (Cr 1 ) exhibited superior mechanical properties, especially in terms of its exceptional hardness, high-temperature oxidation resistance and outstanding corrosion resistance. The average hardness of the WVTaTiCr alloy coating reaches 627.36 HV. After 50 h of high-temperature oxidation, the oxide weight of WVTaTiCr increases by 5.12 m
